title: Removing an endometrial polyp
what: The doctor passes a thin camera into the uterus through the cervix and removes the polyp. There are no cuts on the belly.
why: When a polyp is seen on ultrasound, for spotting between periods, heavy periods, or infertility.
duration: the procedure usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; you often go home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
If you had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The procedure is usually done in the first half of the cycle, after your period. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Swabs, blood tests, and sometimes an ECG. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: If you have anesthesia, you usually do not eat or drink for several hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Bring someone with you. You cannot drive after anesthesia.

steps: You change, and an IV line is placed in your vein
Usually you get short anesthesia through the vein
You lie on the exam chair
The doctor passes the camera through the cervix
The polyp is found and removed
The tissue is sent for testing
You rest in your room for 1 to 2 hours
feel: After the procedure, you may feel pulling low in your belly, like during a period
Light bleeding may last a few days
You may feel sleepy after anesthesia
after: Use pads, not tampons, while you are bleeding
No sauna, bath, swimming pool, or sex. Your doctor will tell you for how long
Polyp test results usually take 1 to 2 weeks
Your doctor will tell you when to come back
red_flags: Severe pain low in your belly

faq.a: Sometimes, yes. That is why follow-up checkups matter.
The procedure is usually done under anesthesia, so you feel nothing.

reminders.text: Polyp removal tomorrow. Bring pads and someone to go with you. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
